goals.goal: Make handtools the one place the user's agent skills (build-skills, untangle, foundation, simple-by-design, remember) are maintained and published, so that (1) pi, Claude Code and Codex install them from one source and flag or apply updates like a plugin/extension, and (2) architecture shared by several skills (untangle + simple-by-design best-practice rules; the meaning and format of an 'ADR' in simple-by-design and foundation) has one source of truth that skills point to instead of copying.
constraints: Skills today live as separate folders under ~/Projects/pi-skills; simple-by-design, remember, foundation and build-skills are separate git repos (remember and simple-by-design have GitHub remotes under sij0sh), untangle has no repo.

Installs are currently hand-made symlinks: ~/.agents/skills (build-skills, foundation, remember, simple-by-design, readme) and ~/.claude/skills (remember, simple-by-design, readme, saaw). Codex has none. Nothing flags updates.
Node/npx is not installed on this machine, so the Vercel Skills CLI suggested in .agents/artifacts/concepts.md is not usable without adding a Node toolchain.
Each harness must load a standard SKILL.md folder with name/description frontmatter.

Use each harness's native packaging where it exists: Claude plugin marketplace, pi git package (pi 1.5.0: pi install/update <source>), and Codex's native plugins (codex plugin marketplace add/upgrade, codex plugin add). pi and Codex both load ~/.agents/skills, and pi keeps the first skill on a name collision, so no handtools skill may also be installed there.

untangle already depends on simple-by-design at run time: its inventory stage asks for an absolute 'policy_root' to an installed simple-by-design and loads references/defaults.md, contract.md, instructions.md and languages/*.md from it (untangle/scripts/workflowlib/ledger.py:13).

'ADR' means two different things today: foundation writes Markdown ADRs in docs/adr/NNNN-*.md from assets/adr-template.md; simple-by-design keeps .agents/design/decisions.json (schema in references/decisions.schema.json) and never uses the word ADR.
build-skills ships templates/workflow/scripts/workflowlib, which untangle and foundation copied; cli.py and storage.py have since drifted between them.
Installed skills may live in a harness cache whose path includes the version and is pruned, so nothing may store an absolute skill path across runs.
Keep it simple: no custom package manager; prefer each harness's native install/update mechanism.
criteria: One command per harness installs all skills from handtools, and one command (or the harness's own prompt) shows an available update after a new version is pushed.
Each shared rule set (defaults, contracts, semantic instructions, language profiles, ADR format) exists in exactly one file in the repo; no second editable copy exists.
untangle finds simple-by-design's rules without the user typing an absolute path.
simple-by-design and foundation use one written definition of an ADR (fields, status values, location), and each skill's output conforms to it.
A check (test or CI) fails if a shared file is copied and edited, or if an installed skill references a shared file that is not present.

decisions.question: Repository shape: one monorepo (handtools) holding all skills, or keep per-skill repos and add an index?
decisions.answer: One monorepo: handtools with skills/<name>/ for build-skills, untangle, foundation, simple-by-design, remember. Repo-level README, CHANGELOG, VERSION, tests/ and harness manifests sit at the root.
decisions.rationale: The goal is literally one place; shared files and one release need one tree. An index over five repos would keep five release flows and cross-repo drift.

decisions.question: Distribution and update mechanism per harness (pi, Claude Code, Codex): native package/plugin systems, the Vercel Skills CLI, or a small local sync script?
decisions.answer: Native per harness (user choice). The repo ships Claude, Codex and pi manifests that all point at skills/ (exact files and install commands in D19). Updates: Claude's /plugin UI flags them. pi is updated with `pi update git:github.com/sij0sh/handtools` (plain `pi update` only updates pi). Codex is updated with `codex plugin marketplace upgrade`. scripts/check.py (stdlib) is the update flag for pi, Codex and the dev checkout (D20): it git-fetches each installed handtools clone and prints 'update available: run <command>' for any that are behind origin. Nothing is symlinked into ~/.agents/skills or ~/.claude/skills.
decisions.rationale: User choices: native installs, a Codex plugin manifest, and check.py as the flag where the harness has none. No symlinks, which avoids pi's duplicate-name collision.

decisions.question: Versioning: one version for the whole repo or per-skill VERSION files, and what triggers an 'update available'?
decisions.answer: One version for the repo: root VERSION, with CHANGELOG.md headings '## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD' (format pi recognises). The Claude plugin, Codex plugin and package.json versions equal VERSION. Release = the maintainer bumps VERSION, adds one changelog entry, pushes. CI fails when files under skills/ change against the last release tag without a VERSION bump. Claude auto-update stays at Claude's default (off for third-party marketplaces): /plugin flags the update and the user applies it. Per-skill VERSION files are removed; any code that read a skill's VERSION reads the root VERSION instead (see D14).
decisions.rationale: Claude only updates on a version change, so an unbumped release would be invisible; CI enforces it. 'Flag, then install' matches the user's plugin-like request.

decisions.question: Where do shared rule files live in the source tree, and who owns each one?
decisions.answer: simple-by-design owns the shared rules: references/defaults.md, references/contract.md, references/instructions.md, languages/*.md (top level of the skill, not under references/), and references/decisions.schema.json (the ADR definition, see D6). Other skills read them; no top-level shared/ dir.
decisions.rationale: One owner (defaults #2). simple-by-design is the design-rules skill and untangle already consumes these exact files from it (existing convention). Shared files inside the owning skill travel with every bundle install, with no extra folder to package.

decisions.question: How does an installed skill reach a shared file, given harnesses install single skill folders: build-time copy into each skill, symlink, or a runtime lookup of a sibling skill?
decisions.answer: Runtime sibling lookup. A consumer finds the owner at <own skill dir resolved through symlinks>/../simple-by-design. Scripts use Path(__file__).resolve(); SKILL.md prose cites paths relative to the skill dir (../simple-by-design/...). If the sibling is missing, fail fast with 'install the handtools bundle' instead of searching elsewhere. untangle's inventory drops the required policy_root; it is resolved automatically, with an optional override.
decisions.rationale: Every D2 install ships the whole skills/ dir as one plugin or package, so the skills are always siblings. No copies are generated, so none can drift. It keeps untangle's existing contract and only removes the manual path.

decisions.question: What is the one ADR definition: Markdown files in docs/adr, the decisions.json record, or a canonical model with one rendering of the other?
decisions.answer: An ADR is a decision row in the project's committed .agents/design/decisions.json (user choice). references/decisions.schema.json in simple-by-design is the one ADR definition: goal = decision context (goal, constraints, criteria), decision row = question, answer, rationale, after. foundation records, audits and validates ADRs in that file. foundation's assets/adr-template.md and the Markdown ADR wording are removed.
decisions.rationale: User chose decisions.json as the ADR log. One schema file is the single source of truth for both skills.

decisions.question: Does the drifted workflowlib (build-skills template copied into untangle and foundation) become shared source too, or stay out of scope?
decisions.answer: Out of scope. The drifted workflowlib copies (build-skills template, untangle, foundation) stay as they are; the user will start a separate design session for them.
decisions.rationale: User choice; the stateless/stateful drift may be deliberate and needs its own analysis.

decisions.question: Drift guard: what check enforces one source of truth and complete installs, and where does it run?
decisions.answer: Stdlib unittest suite in handtools/tests, run locally (`python3 -m unittest`) and in GitHub Actions on push/PR. Checks: (a) every ../<skill>/... path cited in any SKILL.md, reference or script resolves inside skills/; (b) no file outside skills/simple-by-design has the same normalised content hash as a shared rule file (content only, never basename: build-skills/references/instructions.md is a different file with the same name); (c) VERSION equals all three manifest versions, and skills/ changes need a bump (D3); (d) the keys, required fields, enums and ID patterns in decisions.schema.json match what record.py validates (derived from the schema file in the test), and every committed decisions.json passes record.py's validation; (e) each skill's own test suite runs: stdlib skills on one OS; remember keeps its 3-OS matrix with `pip install -r skills/remember/requirements.txt`, moved into the root workflow.
decisions.rationale: Reviewer findings: basename matching false-positives on day one; the schema and record.py are two sources unless a test ties them; remember's nested CI would stop running.

decisions.question: Migration: how do existing repos' history and the current hand-made symlinks move to handtools?
decisions.answer: Import with history: `git subtree add --prefix=skills/<name>` from each local repo (simple-by-design, remember, foundation, build-skills); untangle is added as new files. Each skill's .agents/ working notes are not imported. Each skill's nested .github/ moves into the root workflow (D8e); per-skill tool configs (foundation's ruff.toml, mise.toml, .gitignore) stay inside their skill. foundation's docs/adr/0001-0002 become a goal in handtools' .agents/design/decisions.json via designflow.py record. Old symlinks are swapped out per harness as in D22. The old GitHub repos are left alone; the user archives them when ready.
decisions.rationale: Keeps history at low cost and changes no installs before the new ones are verified. Archiving remote repos is an outward action for the user.

decisions.question: Does the decisions.json schema need ADR lifecycle fields that foundation's Markdown ADRs had (date, superseded, retroactive)?
decisions.answer: Add two optional fields to a decision: 'date' and 'superseded_by'. Add 'superseded' to the status enum. Status stays derived, never sent: open without an answer, resolved with an answer, superseded when superseded_by is set. apply_payload stamps 'date' (YYYY-MM-DD) the first time a row resolves, so both done and record set it. References to another goal use 'G#/D#' in both 'after' and 'superseded_by'; a bare D# means the same goal. open_rows treats superseded rows as closed, and the renderer shows them marked superseded. Each change goes into both decisions.schema.json and record.py, and the D8(d) test keeps them equal. Retroactive decisions need no extra field: foundation records them under a goal like 'Record decisions already in the code', with rationale left out when unknown.
decisions.rationale: Only the fields foundation already uses; nothing speculative.

decisions.question: Who writes decisions.json when foundation records an ADR?
decisions.answer: designflow.py is the only writer. A new command `designflow.py [--root DIR] record [--goal G#]` (--root is the existing global option and defaults to the cwd). It reads a payload shaped like `done`'s and upserts one goal (a new G# when --goal is left out). New rows get IDs from the existing next_id, and dates and status follow D10. It validates with record.py and writes under the existing lock. It loads sessions with allow_missing=True and refuses when an active session holds that goal. foundation's apply stage calls python3 S/../simple-by-design/scripts/designflow.py --root <project root> record. Nothing else edits the file directly.
decisions.rationale: One owner for mutable state (defaults #2; contract.md access through the owner). It reuses the existing payload contract and lock.

decisions.question: decisions.json is currently gitignored in several repos (.agents/ in .gitignore). How does the ADR log get committed?
decisions.answer: decisions.json is committed; only .agents/design/workflow.json and .agents/artifacts/ are ignored. The .gitignore pattern that works is '.agents/*', '!.agents/design/', '.agents/design/*', '!.agents/design/decisions.json'. In handtools, also '!.agents/plugins/' if Codex needs its marketplace file there (D19). simple-by-design warns at close and on record when decisions.json is ignored or untracked, and prints the pattern; it never edits .gitignore. foundation lists the .gitignore fix as an item to approve in assess, applies it on approval, and validate.py fails while decisions.json is ignored or untracked.
decisions.rationale: User choice. git cannot re-include a file under an ignored directory, so the exact pattern has to be written down.

decisions.question: What does foundation do in a target project that already has Markdown ADRs in docs/adr?
decisions.answer: audit counts existing docs/adr/*.md or docs/decisions/*.md as having ADRs and reports it. foundation records new decisions only in decisions.json. It converts existing Markdown ADRs into decisions.json only when the user approves that item in assess.
decisions.rationale: Changing a project convention needs an explicit decision. Converting by default would rewrite user documents.

decisions.question: How does untangle's stored policy (root path plus simple-by-design VERSION) survive plugin updates that move the cache path, and the removal of per-skill VERSION?
decisions.answer: untangle resolves the simple-by-design sibling again on every run and resume; it never reuses a stored path, and an optional override applies only to that one run. Drift detection compares content hashes of the policy files only. The recorded version comes from the root VERSION, for information only, never as a drift trigger. A policy file that is missing at resume time is a hard error naming the file, not an empty policy.
decisions.rationale: A cached plugin path includes the version and is pruned, so a stored absolute root goes stale. Hashes are what actually detect rule drift.

decisions.question: Codex ignores 'disable-model-invocation'. How do build-skills, untangle and foundation stay explicit-only in every harness?
decisions.answer: Keep 'disable-model-invocation: true' in their SKILL.md (Claude, pi) and add agents/openai.yaml with policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false to each (Codex), following remember's existing agents/openai.yaml. A D8 test checks that the two settings agree for every skill under skills/, including any skill build-skills creates later (D23). In Claude the commands become /handtools:<skill>; directory names are unchanged, so D5's ../ lookup still holds.
decisions.rationale: Each harness reads its own flag; a test stops the two from drifting.

decisions.question: Which foundation files change for the ADR switch?
decisions.answer: SKILL.md and README stop mentioning Markdown ADRs. assets/adr-template.md is removed. greenfield.md: record the stack choice as a goal through designflow.py record. brownfield.md: record decisions already in the code with rationale left out when unknown, replacing 'Status: accepted (retroactive)'. audit.py: 'adrs' is present when .agents/design/decisions.json has at least one resolved decision, or when legacy docs/adr/*.md or docs/decisions/*.md exist (reported as legacy, D13). validate.py: validate decisions.json through simple-by-design's record.py, check that it is tracked (D12), and keep the title check only for legacy Markdown files. workflowlib/steps.py baseline text: 'Important decisions recorded in .agents/design/decisions.json'.
decisions.rationale: Lists every reference found to the old format, so nothing is left half-migrated.

decisions.question: How do people read ADRs without the tools?
decisions.answer: Add a read-only `designflow.py [--root DIR] show [--goal G#]`. It prints every goal, or one goal, as Markdown: goal, constraints, criteria, then each decision with D# id, question, answer, rationale, after, date, and superseded_by when present. The goal renderer moves out of steps.summary into one function that both show and the close summary call. No generated file is committed.
decisions.rationale: User choice. One source with a view on demand, so there is no copy to drift.

decisions.question: How does an agent resolve paths written in SKILL.md prose, both to the skill's own scripts and to sibling skills?
decisions.answer: Every SKILL.md begins its run steps the way remember does: 'Set S to this skill's absolute directory.' Own scripts are cited as S/scripts/..., the shared rules as S/../simple-by-design/... This replaces 'From the project root, drive the run with scripts/...' in foundation, untangle and build-skills; the project root stays the cwd. D8(a) checks the cited paths.
decisions.rationale: Agents otherwise resolve relative paths from the project root.

decisions.question: Which marketplace and plugin manifests does the repo ship, and where does the plugin root sit?
decisions.answer: The plugin root is the repo root: .claude-plugin/plugin.json (name 'handtools', version = VERSION) and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (marketplace name 'handtools', one plugin with source './'), .codex-plugin/plugin.json ('skills': './skills/'), and package.json with the 'pi' manifest. Codex reuses .claude-plugin/marketplace.json if implementation testing shows it accepts that file; otherwise also add .agents/plugins/marketplace.json (and un-ignore it, D12). If either harness rejects a plugin source of './', move the plugin to plugins/handtools/ with skills/ inside it; sibling paths do not change. Install commands: Claude `/plugin marketplace add sij0sh/handtools` then `/plugin install handtools@handtools`; Codex `codex plugin marketplace add sij0sh/handtools` then `codex plugin add handtools@handtools`; pi `pi install git:github.com/sij0sh/handtools`. D8(c) checks every manifest version against VERSION.
decisions.rationale: Pins the names that every install command depends on. The fallbacks cover the two Codex behaviours this session could not confirm, without reopening the design.

decisions.question: What is the update flag for Codex, which has no command that only checks?
decisions.answer: Same as pi (follows the user's pi choice): scripts/check.py also compares Codex's cached handtools marketplace clone with origin and prints 'update available: run codex plugin marketplace upgrade'. Codex auto-upgrade for the marketplace is left off, so updates are flagged and then applied by the user.
decisions.rationale: Keeps one 'flag, then you apply' behaviour across all three harnesses, as the user chose for Claude and pi. The user can switch Codex auto-upgrade on at any time.

decisions.question: How does the maintainer test local edits in each harness without pushing?
decisions.answer: The README documents local-source installs: `claude --plugin-dir /abs/handtools`, `pi install /abs/handtools` (a local path is live), and `codex plugin marketplace add /abs/handtools` (cached, so run upgrade or reinstall after edits). No symlinks.
decisions.rationale: Replaces the live-edit loop the old symlinks gave, using each harness's own local-source support.

decisions.question: When are the old symlinks removed, given that old copies in ~/.agents/skills would hide the new install in pi (and Codex)?
decisions.answer: Per harness, right before verifying that harness: remove the old symlinks for the five skills from the dirs that harness reads (~/.agents/skills for pi and Codex, ~/.claude/skills for Claude), install handtools, and confirm the five skills load from the new location. If verification fails, put the symlinks back. readme and saaw stay untouched. This step amends D9's 'after the installs work'.
decisions.rationale: Verification is only meaningful once the old copies cannot shadow the new ones.

decisions.question: Does build-skills need to know the bundle conventions?
decisions.answer: Yes. When build-skills creates or revises a skill, it writes agents/openai.yaml with allow_implicit_invocation equal to the inverse of disable-model-invocation, and it uses D18's 'Set S' path wording. It does not copy the shared rule files. Its prompts cite them through S/../simple-by-design/ when needed.
decisions.rationale: Otherwise every skill build-skills produces fails the D15 and D8(a) tests.

decisions.question: What happens to per-skill CHANGELOG.md files?
decisions.answer: build-skills' and simple-by-design's CHANGELOG.md files fold into the root CHANGELOG.md, with their existing entries kept unchanged under a '### <skill> (pre-handtools)' heading below the first handtools release. The per-skill files are removed.
decisions.rationale: One version needs one changelog (D3). Old entries are kept, not rewritten.

goals.goal: foundation skill: decisions already in its code (converted from foundation docs/adr 0001-0002, accepted retroactively 2026-11-06).
constraints: The skill is run by an agent inside other repositories; a run may span several agent executions.

decisions.question: Should foundation's workflow keep per-project run state?
decisions.answer: No. workflowlib/steps.py sets MODE = 'stateless'. start prints the first stage, and each `done --stage S` names the finished stage, validates its JSON payload, and prints the next. The orchestrator carries earlier results forward; no state is written. There is no resume, status, or abandon for a run; every stage must receive the user's request and the earlier stages' results.
decisions.rationale: The target repository should not accumulate per-project workflow state; re-running a stage is safe because stages only read until apply. (Was docs/adr/0001-stateless-workflow.md.)

decisions.question: May foundation's scripts use third-party Python packages?
decisions.answer: No. audit.py, validate.py, workflow.py and workflowlib/ import only the Python standard library (3.9+). Optional checks degrade to `skipped` when tomllib (3.11+) or PyYAML is unavailable. tests/test_imports.py enforces it; mise pins only the development toolchain.
decisions.rationale: scripts/ ships with the skill and must run without an install step. (Was docs/adr/0002-stdlib-only-python.md.)

goals.goal: Consolidate the uncommitted state the handtools workflow skills (build-skills, foundation, simple-by-design, untangle) read and write into one per-user root, ~/.agents/state (platform equivalent on macOS/Windows), with a decisions/ area shared by simple-by-design and foundation and areas for build-skills and untangle, each organized by project/repo, keeping today's file shapes and merging schemas where that removes duplication. The ADR log itself stays committed in the project. Phase 2 (separate, after this): DRY the scripts/templates (the copied workflowlib) so new skills reuse one implementation.
constraints: Today state is scattered across 3 conventions: (a) <installed skill dir>/state/<name>-<sha8 of root path>/workflow.json for build-skills and untangle (foundation's workflowlib is stateless); (b) <repo>/.agents/design/{decisions.json, workflow.json, workflow.lock} for simple-by-design; (c) <repo>/.agents/foundation.json (kind, maturity, decisions, accepted, declined, updated) and <repo>/.agents/artifacts/untangle/<audit-id>/{current.md, audit.json, report.md} as derived exports.

State inside the installed skill dir is unsafe: G1 constraint says plugin caches are versioned and pruned (e.g. ~/.claude/plugins/cache/handtools/handtools/0.0.1/...), so an update silently loses in-progress build-skills/untangle runs. An orphan skills/untangle/state/ut-7769e103/ already sits in this repo checkout.

Adopted G1 decisions D6/D11/D12: the ADR log is the project's COMMITTED .agents/design/decisions.json, written only by designflow.py (done/record); foundation and validate.py require it tracked in git. Moving it to ~/.agents/state would reverse these and take ADRs out of the repo (not reviewable in PRs, lost to other clones/teammates).

storage.py/cli.py/flow.py are copied verbatim (by md5) across build-skills template, foundation and untangle; build-skills' own build_skills/storage.py equals the template copy; simple-by-design has its own variant with a different lock path. project_root()/project_key()/lock()/write_json() are duplicated 4x.
~/.agents/skills is read by pi and Codex as a skills dir; ~/.agents/state is a sibling, not under skills/, so harnesses will not scan it.
Python 3.9+ stdlib only; Linux, macOS, Windows.
Keep current per-skill file shapes (workflow.json session registries, untangle's audit state) unless a merge removes a real duplicate.
criteria: Every non-committed run/session state for the four skills lives under one per-user root with one documented layout: <root>/<area>/<project-key>/...; no skill writes state into its own install dir.
One function computes the state root and project key; every skill uses it (no second copy).
A plugin update or reinstall does not lose an in-progress run.
The ADR log location and commit policy are explicit and consistent with (or explicitly supersede) G1 D6/D12.
Existing state (this repo's .agents/design/workflow.json, the stray untangle state) has a stated migration or is knowingly dropped.
Tests cover root resolution per OS (incl. an override env var) and project-key stability.

decisions.question: ADR log: does the committed <repo>/.agents/design/decisions.json move into ~/.agents/state/decisions/<project>/ (superseding G1 D6/D12), or stay in the repo with only uncommitted session/run state moving to ~/.agents/state?
decisions.answer: Keep it in the project. The ADR log stays the committed <repo>/.agents/design/decisions.json, written only by designflow.py (done/record) and defined by references/decisions.schema.json; G1/D6, G1/D11 and G1/D12 stand unchanged (gitcheck warnings, foundation's `adrs` capability, audit.py/validate.py tracking checks all stay). Only uncommitted state moves: simple-by-design's workflow.json session registry and workflow.lock go to ~/.agents/state/decisions/<key>/. designflow takes that one lock around writes to both files.
decisions.rationale: User choice (revised): decisions stay reviewable in PRs and shared with every clone; session state is per-user scratch and belongs outside the repo.

decisions.question: State root per OS and override: Path.home()/.agents/state on every OS, XDG/Library/AppData per platform, and which env var overrides it?
decisions.answer: Path.home() / '.agents' / 'state' on every OS (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.agents\state), overridden by env HANDTOOLS_STATE (absolute path, used as the root itself). No XDG/AppData branching.
decisions.rationale: Matches the user's request and the existing ~/.agents/skills convention pi and Codex already use on all three OSes; one code path. The env var lets tests and unusual setups redirect without code changes.

decisions.question: Project key under each area: keep today's <dirname>-<sha8 of resolved root path>, or derive from the git remote URL (shared across clones/worktrees)?
decisions.answer: Keep today's key: <sanitized dirname>-<first 8 hex of sha256(normcase(resolved project root))>, root = --root, else git top level, else cwd. Each <area>/<key>/ dir also gets project.json {"root": "<abs path>"} written on first use so a human (and `status`) can tell which repo a key belongs to. Moving or renaming a repo orphans only its in-progress session/run state (the ADR log travels with the repo, D1); the fix is a manual `mv` of the key dir (documented), no remap command.
decisions.rationale: User choice. project.json makes an orphaned key diagnosable without adding remote-URL logic.

decisions.question: What lives in decisions/<project>/: simple-by-design's session registry (workflow.json) plus what of foundation's .agents/foundation.json (kind, maturity, topic->answer decisions, accepted/declined item ids)? Do foundation's topic->answer decisions merge into the ADR schema instead of a second decisions shape?
decisions.answer: decisions/<key>/ holds simple-by-design's workflow.json (unchanged shape), workflow.lock, project.json, and foundation.json. The ADR log is not here (D1). Schema merge: foundation's interview answers (today a topic->answer dict in .agents/foundation.json, plus kind and maturity) become ADR rows in the committed decisions.json, recorded through `designflow.py record` under one foundation goal. foundation.json shrinks to foundation's own bookkeeping: {"goal": "G#", "accepted": [ids], "declined": [ids], "updated": "YYYY-MM-DD"}.
decisions.rationale: One owner for decisions (defaults #2): the same fact no longer lives in two shapes in two files. accepted/declined are capability-item bookkeeping, not decisions, so they stay foundation's and per-user.

decisions.question: untangle's derived exports (.agents/artifacts/untangle/<audit-id>/current.md, audit.json, report.md): move under state/untangle/<project>/ next to the run state, or stay in the repo?
decisions.answer: Move them: untangle writes current.md, audit.json, report.md to ~/.agents/state/untangle/<key>/<audit-id>/, beside workflow.json, and prints the absolute path of report.md/current.md in each step. Nothing is written under the target repo.
decisions.rationale: User choice; keeps audited repos clean and removes the .agents/artifacts .gitignore entries.

decisions.question: Area naming and layout rule for build-skills, untangle, and future skills generated from build-skills' template: <root>/<area>/<project-key>/ with area = skill name except the shared 'decisions' area? Per-area lock?
decisions.answer: Layout: <root>/<area>/<key>/. area = the skill's AREA constant (D10): the skill name for build-skills, untangle, and any skill generated from build-skills' template; simple-by-design and foundation share area `decisions`. One workflow.lock per <area>/<key>/ dir, same mkdir lock and stale timeout as today, guarding script writes only (foundation.json is agent-written, D9). No skill writes into its own install dir; the generated-skill .gitignore 'state/' line and the template docstring change accordingly.
decisions.rationale: The user's proposed layout; area-per-skill keeps skills from colliding without a registry, and the shared area is exactly the one shared owner of decisions.

decisions.question: Where does the single state-root/project-key/lock/write_json implementation live so all four skills import one copy (owned by one sibling skill vs a shared folder), or is that deferred to phase 2 with only the layout fixed now?
decisions.answer: Fix the layout and contract now; the single implementation lands in phase 2. Contract of the one module: state_root() -> Path (HANDTOOLS_STATE or ~/.agents/state); project_root(arg) -> Path; project_key(root) -> str; state_dir(area, root) -> Path (creates it and project.json); read_json/write_json(atomic); lock(dir). Phase 2 picks its home and how the 4 skills plus the template import it (G1/D7's deferred workflowlib session). Until then each existing storage.py copy is edited identically, and the bundle test asserts the copies are byte-equal so they cannot drift in the meantime.
decisions.rationale: The user split the work into two phases; where shared code lives is the core phase-2 question (G1/D7 deferred it). An equality test keeps criterion 'one function, no drifting copy' honest in the interim.

decisions.question: Migration of existing state (this repo's .agents/design/workflow.json with sessions s1/s2, stray skills/untangle/state/, any <installed skill>/state dirs): automatic move on first run, one-off manual move, or drop?
decisions.answer: One-off manual move, no migration code. On this machine: move handtools' .agents/design/workflow.json to ~/.agents/state/decisions/<handtools key>/ (decisions.json stays where it is, committed); delete the stray skills/untangle/state/ and any <installed skill>/state dirs (in-progress runs only, already exposed to cache pruning). CHANGELOG notes, for any other user, the one `mv` per project for workflow.json and .agents/foundation.json. Bump the version (G1/D3).
decisions.rationale: Simplest adequate: one known user, a handful of files; permanent legacy-path code would outlive its one use.

decisions.question: Who writes foundation.json now that it lives outside the repo? Today the agent writes .agents/foundation.json itself in apply, so a script lock cannot cover it.
decisions.answer: The agent still writes it, at the absolute path foundation's steps.py prints, computed through storage.state_dir('decisions', root). No lock: foundation's apply step is its only writer, and designflow.py never touches it. This corrects D6's 'under that dir's lock' clause: the lock guards only designflow's decisions.json/workflow.json writes. check_apply reads the same path and requires goal, accepted, declined, updated.
decisions.rationale: Same writer as today, only the location changes; the agent cannot take a script-held lock.

decisions.question: How does a skill name its area: a constant in code, or derived from its install folder name?
decisions.answer: An explicit constant: AREA = 'decisions' in simple-by-design and foundation, 'untangle', 'build-skills'. The template's steps.py declares AREA beside MODE, and build-skills sets it to the new skill's name when it copies the template.
decisions.rationale: Local reasoning (defaults #3): the reader sees the area in the code. Install folder names can differ by harness.

decisions.question: Does the bundle test change now that workflow.json leaves the repo?
decisions.answer: The bundle test keeps both G1/D8d checks (schema vs record.py, and every committed decisions.json validates). Tests never read the real ~/.agents/state; they set HANDTOOLS_STATE to a temp dir. No supersession is recorded against G1.
decisions.rationale: With the ADR log still committed (D1), G1's decisions stand as written.

decisions.question: How does foundation's interview find the decisions it already recorded once they live in decisions.json?
decisions.answer: foundation.json.goal names its goal. Interview runs `designflow.py show` and treats that goal's resolved rows as settled; apply records new and changed answers with `designflow.py record --goal <that G#>` (no --goal on first run, then stores the new G# in foundation.json). kind and maturity are rows in that goal, questions 'Project kind' and 'Maturity'.
decisions.rationale: Completes D4's merge with the existing record command; no new command.

goals.goal: Phase 2 of G3: give the workflow engine code shared by build-skills, foundation, simple-by-design, untangle and build-skills' workflow template one implementation (DRY), so a fix or new capability lands once and new workflow skills reuse it instead of copying.
constraints: Byte-identical copies today (guarded by tests/test_bundle.py StateTest): storage.py x5 (template, build_skills, foundation, untangle, designlib), cli.py x4 (template, build_skills, foundation, untangle), flow.py x3 (template, foundation, untangle), launcher workflow.py x3 (template, foundation, untangle).

Near-duplicates that drifted: simple-by-design's designflow.py reimplements cli.py (quote, launcher, read_payload, error printing); multi-session registries in designlib/sessions.py (164 lines, with legacy-shape migration and goal holders) and build_skills/sessions.py (71 lines) share find/active/select_active/close/timestamp/load/save with small differences in messages and fields.

Two engine shapes exist: single-run flow (template/foundation/untangle: start/status/done/abandon, MODE stateful|stateless) and multi-session registry (simple-by-design, build-skills: s1..sN, --session, status --all).
The engine's flow.py does `from . import steps`: each skill's steps.py lives inside its copy of the workflowlib package, so the package cannot be shared as-is.

build-skills writes new skills to any target path, including outside handtools (e.g. ~/.agents/skills/readme); such a skill cannot assume a handtools sibling, so the template must still produce a self-contained engine (or explicitly require handtools installed).

Distribution (G1/D2, D5): every harness installs the whole repo (pi: package.json pi.skills ./skills; Claude and Codex plugins: skills ./skills/). Skills reach shared files as siblings at S/../<skill>/; G1/D4 put shared rules inside an owning skill and chose no top-level shared/ dir.
Installed plugin paths are versioned caches; nothing may store an absolute skill path across runs (G1/D14). Python 3.9+ stdlib only; Linux, macOS, Windows.

Out of scope: remember (separate engine), and changing the state layout fixed in G3 phase 1. Open from phase 1: designflow resolves the project root as cwd while the others use git top level (same key only when run from the repo root).
criteria: Each shared engine behavior (state paths/lock/JSON, CLI helpers, single-run flow, session registry) has exactly one editable implementation inside handtools; the byte-equality guard is replaced by imports, or kept only where a copy is unavoidable and justified.
Adding a new workflow skill inside handtools needs only its steps (prompts, checks, advance) plus a thin launcher.
build-skills can still generate a working workflow skill outside handtools.
All four skills resolve the project root the same way.
Every existing test suite still passes; behavior and state files are unchanged for users.

decisions.question: Where does the one engine implementation live: inside an owning skill (build-skills' templates/workflow, since it already is the canonical engine), a new non-skill folder under skills/ (e.g. skills/_engine/), or a top-level lib/ beside skills/?
decisions.answer: skills/_engine/: a plain Python package (no SKILL.md) holding the one engine: storage.py, cli.py, flow.py (single run), sessions.py (multi-session registry), __init__.py. Imported as `_engine` (`from _engine import cli, flow, storage`). build-skills' templates/workflow/ keeps only the launcher and an example steps.py. Explicitly supersedes G1/D4's 'no top-level shared/ dir' for engine code only; shared design rules stay owned by simple-by-design.
decisions.rationale: User choice: a neutral owner rather than making three skills depend on build-skills.

decisions.question: How does a skill import the shared engine at run time: insert the resolved sibling path into sys.path from its launcher (like untangle's policy lookup), or something else; and what happens when it is missing?
decisions.answer: Each launcher (workflow.py, designflow.py, build-skills.py, the template's workflow.py) finds the engine by walking up from its own resolved path to the first ancestor that holds _engine/__init__.py, puts that ancestor on sys.path, then runs `from _engine import ...`. This finds a vendored <scripts>/_engine first (D6), else skills/_engine from any depth inside handtools (skill scripts and build-skills/templates/workflow/scripts alike). If none is found it prints 'ERROR: engine not found; install the handtools bundle' and exits 2. It's a ~4-line block per launcher, not a shared helper, because it has to run before the engine is importable.
decisions.rationale: Same sibling-at-run-time rule as G1/D5, with one fail-fast message. Resolving from __file__ every run keeps it valid across versioned caches (G1/D14).

decisions.question: How does the shared single-run flow reach each skill's steps (today `from . import steps` inside the package): pass the steps module into flow functions, or a registration call from the launcher?
decisions.answer: Pass the steps module explicitly: flow.start(steps, root, launcher), status/done/abandon likewise; flow reads steps.MODE, steps.AREA, steps.ORDER, PROMPTS, CHECKS, advance, DONE_MSG. Each skill's steps live in its own package or module (untangle keeps workflowlib/ with steps, checks, ledger, work, transitions, exports; foundation keeps workflowlib/steps.py; the template ships scripts/steps.py).
decisions.rationale: Local reasoning (defaults #3): the dependency is an argument a reader can see, not a relative import into another skill's package.

decisions.question: Do the two multi-session registries (simple-by-design, build-skills) merge into one shared sessions module, and how do skill-specific fields (simple-by-design's goal/cycle/baseline, legacy migration, holders) extend it?
decisions.answer: One _engine/sessions.py with the generic registry both skills duplicate: path(area, root), load(area, root, allow_missing), save, add(state, **fields) (next sN id, status active, created/updated timestamps), find, active, select_active, close(session, status), timestamp. Skill-specific fields stay with the skill: simple-by-design's validate/_normalize legacy migration, goal holders and its phase field names; build-skills' root/target fields. One shared message wording ('pass --session sN').
decisions.rationale: One owner per behavior; skill rules stay local so the shared module does not grow per-skill options.

decisions.question: Does designflow.py adopt the shared cli.py helpers and the shared project_root (git top level, else cwd), changing its --root default from cwd?
decisions.answer: Yes. designflow.py uses _engine.cli (quote, launcher, read_payload, run) and _engine.storage.project_root, so --root defaults to the git top level, else cwd, like the other skills; foundation's steps resolve the root the same way instead of Path.cwd(). The help text and CHANGELOG note the changed default.
decisions.rationale: Criterion: all four skills resolve the project root the same way; removes designflow's second CLI implementation.

decisions.question: What does build-skills give a skill generated outside handtools: a vendored copy of the engine (copied at generation time, never edited in place), or a dependency on an installed handtools?
decisions.answer: Vendored copy. When build-skills installs or revises a workflow skill, it copies skills/_engine/ (located as its own sibling) into <target>/scripts/_engine/, replacing any previous copy and never touching the skill's steps. The vendored copy is never edited in place; revising the skill refreshes it.
decisions.rationale: User choice: skills outside handtools keep working without handtools installed.

decisions.question: Which guards replace the byte-equality test: an import-only check (no skill outside the owner defines storage/cli/flow), and how are generated vendored copies kept current?
decisions.answer: Replace StateTest's byte-equality with: (a) inside skills/, storage.py, cli.py, flow.py, sessions.py and a scripts/_engine/ folder exist only under skills/_engine/; (b) every launcher's engine lookup resolves to skills/_engine in the repo; (c) the _engine tests (moved from StateTest plus flow/sessions unit tests) run in CI. Vendored copies outside handtools are refreshed only by build-skills revise (D6); no version stamp.
decisions.rationale: Import, not compare: no copy left to drift inside the repo.

decisions.question: Do pi, Claude Code and Codex ignore skills/_engine/ (no SKILL.md) without errors or a phantom skill?
decisions.answer: Verify before merging: install the branch locally in each harness (claude --plugin-dir, pi install <path>, codex plugin marketplace add <path>) and confirm exactly the five skills load with no warning about _engine. If one harness complains, stop and bring it back to the user (fallback: move _engine inside an owner skill).
decisions.rationale: The one untested assumption behind D1.

decisions.question: How do a skill's prompts and checks learn the project root (foundation's foundation.json path is computed at import from cwd; untangle re-parses sys.argv)?
decisions.answer: flow passes it in: every state dict flow hands to checks and advance carries 'root' (stateful runs already store it; stateless runs get {'phase': stage, 'root': str(root)}), and a PROMPTS value may be a function of root that flow calls when showing the step. foundation uses both and drops its import-time path. untangle keeps its working sys.argv lookup (out of scope).
decisions.rationale: Removes the import-time side effect and keeps --root authoritative without a global.

decisions.question: Where do the engine's tests live and run?
decisions.answer: skills/_engine/tests/ (storage tests moved from tests/test_bundle.py StateTest, plus flow and sessions unit tests). Added to the README check list and the CI workflow next to the other skill suites. The bundle test keeps only the D7 structure guards, and its sibling-path regex learns _engine.

goals.goal: v0.1.1 M1 (.agents/artifacts/v011.md): add a shared, non-invokable reconnaissance component in skills/_engine/recon (evidence-backed records of snapshots, components, contracts, relationships, observations, decision references and discovery gaps), record it through the existing SQLite journal with versioned typed reducers, project it into remember, and integrate it into foundation and untangle, so both identify upstream/downstream external contracts with evidence and reuse unchanged evidence safely across source changes.
constraints: Python 3.9+, standard library only; no graph database; no network access or autonomous org-wide discovery; collectors never execute project code.

_engine/recon has no SKILL.md, no invocation trigger and never invokes another skill; it ships inside the existing _engine copy (build_skills/skill.py install_engine already copies the whole directory).

The SQLite journal (_engine/events.py Journal) is the only authority; remember projections, untangle exports (current.md, audit.json, report.md) and reports are rebuildable views. No new maintained JSON/Markdown runtime artifacts.
Existing version-1 journals replay unchanged and are never rewritten; unsupported envelope versions fail visibly; expected-revision checks, request-id idempotency and gap/fork detection are kept.

Foundation stays stateless (discover/interview/assess/apply/validate) and keeps its apply boundaries; untangle keeps its stages, path ledger, budgets and A/B/gap tracks. Recon completeness never implies review coverage.
Inferred observations never become adopted decisions; .agents/design/decisions.json stays the only adopted-decision source.
Unknown contract fields stay unknown; an advertised channel without subscriber evidence is an exposed contract with an unknown consumer, never 'no consumers'.

_engine library code and repo tests are edited directly. foundation and untangle changes go through /handtools:build-skills revise sessions (both are staged skills). remember (script-backed, neither staged nor prompt) and build-skills' own skill.py install_engine are edited directly with unit tests, by user decision (D17).
M1 only drafts the generator manifest (workflow contract); build-skills generation/enforcement is M4. No review/security workflows (M2/M3).
criteria: Fixture (API, scheduled ingestion, queue publisher, shared schema) plus a separately supplied consumer repo, with an explicit expected map: both foundation and untangle runs identify the upstream and downstream contracts and cite evidence.
Repository-only mode records the queue consumer as unknown with a discovery gap; supplying the consumer repository resolves it.
Foundation reports an ownership/compatibility gap; untangle records a downstream behavior constraint.
Changing the shared schema marks affected records and dependent untangle conclusions stale; records whose evidence hashes are unchanged are reused in the successor snapshot.
An inferred pattern stays an observation and is never projected as an adopted decision.
Rebuilding remember projections from the journal reproduces the reduced state; a duplicated receipt adds no record; gaps/forks in the chain raise errors.
All existing tests (skills/*/tests, tests/) pass; untangle exports keep their current shape; a version-1 journal fixture replays identically.
A written M1 comparison report (pre-change vs new outputs against the expected map) records discovery improvements and investigation cost (files read, bytes, records, wall time).

decisions.question: How are recon records written into the journal without breaking version-1 replay?
decisions.answer: Add one event kind, `record.accepted`, whose payload is a versioned envelope {"schema": "handtools.recon", "version": 1, "records": [...]}. events.replay takes an explicit `reducers` argument (envelope schema -> pure reducer); existing kinds keep the generic merge, and a record.accepted event with no matching reducer/version raises. Event protocol schema_version stays 1, so version-1 runs replay byte-identically.
decisions.rationale: Smallest change that gives typed reduction; explicit parameter instead of a global registry keeps events.py domain-free and readable locally.

decisions.question: Where does recon state live and what is a run?
decisions.answer: <state root>/recon/<project key>/events.sqlite3. Each snapshot is one journal run (id `snap-N`): run.started carries the Snapshot record, record.accepted events add or supersede records, run.closed freezes it. Refreshing after source changes or resuming a closed snapshot starts a successor run that references its predecessor and carries forward records whose evidence hashes still match.
decisions.rationale: Reuses Journal append/replay/closure semantics unchanged; successor runs satisfy 'never append past closure'.

decisions.question: How are stable entity IDs and evidence references shaped?
decisions.answer: IDs are `<type>:<natural key>` from agent-supplied identity, never line numbers: `component:<repo>/<name>`, `contract:<kind>:<channel>` (kind = http|queue|schedule|schema|table|file|webhook|sdk; e.g. contract:queue:orders.created), `rel:<type>:<from>-><to>`, `obs:<slug>`, `gap:<slug>`, `decision:<G#>/<D#>`. Direction, producer and consumer are fields, not identity. An unknown endpoint is `{"unresolved": "<role> of <contract id>"}`. Evidence refs are {source: repo label ('.' or a related-repo label), path, sha256 of file content, lines (informational only), statement}. Classification (observed|configured|declared|inferred|unknown) and confidence (high|medium|low) are separate fields. Re-recording an id supersedes it; the reducer keeps the supersession chain. A `decision:` record must resolve to an answered decision in .agents/design/decisions.json or the validator rejects it; inferred patterns and conflicts are observations.
decisions.rationale: Content-derived identity survives line moves; validating decision refs against the ADR log is the one mechanical guard that keeps inferences out of adopted decisions.

decisions.question: What command surface do agents use to collect, record and query recon, and how do its receipts reach transcripts?
decisions.answer: One script, skills/_engine/recon/cli.py (path-bootstrapped like engine.py): read-only `orient` and `candidates` (collector output, never records), and journal commands `start` (snapshot: scope roots incl. explicit `--related label=path`, exclusions, depth, budgets), `record`, `close`, `refresh` (successor run), `status`, `query <name>`. Write commands require --expect-revision and --request-id and print the accepted event as the receipt, same shape as engine.py. recordings.command_is_engine also accepts direct `recon/cli.py record|start|close|refresh` invocations so receipts are transcript-discoverable. A `recon.prompt(root)` (like planning.prompt) owns the progressive-discovery instructions and prints the CLI path; foundation and untangle prompts include it instead of copying text.
decisions.rationale: Mirrors the existing engine.py receipt and planning.prompt conventions; one owner for the recon instructions.

decisions.question: Which collectors exist in M1 and how are orient/map/deepen budgets enforced?
decisions.answer: Two pure, bounded collectors in recon/collect.py, both stdlib and repository-local (plus explicitly supplied related roots): `orient` inventories manifests, entrypoints, config, schemas (OpenAPI/JSON Schema/Avro/proto/GraphQL), migrations, CI, infra (compose/k8s/terraform/cron) and decision sources; `candidates` applies a small fixture-backed pattern table (Python + YAML/JSON config: HTTP routes, schedules, queue publish/subscribe, schema refs, table DDL) and reports other languages as unsupported scope. Both enforce max_files/max_bytes and report truncation as a gap. Map and deepen are agent operations: the snapshot records budgets (files, bytes, traversal depth, allowed_commands default none), each `record` batch carries a `cost` {files, bytes, commands}, the reducer accumulates it and `record` refuses batches that exceed the budget (a successor snapshot with user-approved budget is required). Cost totals feed the comparison report.
decisions.rationale: Collectors produce candidates only; agent-side budgets cannot be measured by the script, so declared cost is accounted and enforced at the recording boundary.

decisions.question: How are staleness and invalidation computed, including dependent workflow conclusions?
decisions.answer: `refresh` rehashes every cited evidence file in the successor run: a record is stale if any evidence hash changed or file vanished; records whose `depends_on` names a stale entity become stale transitively; records with no evidence dependencies (e.g. inferred observations) go stale when the snapshot scope fingerprint (git HEAD + dirty-content hashes, or tree hash outside git) changed — conservative fallback. Unchanged records are carried forward with `reused_from: snap-N@rev`; stale ones are carried as status=stale and must be re-recorded or dropped. Workflow conclusions that cite recon ids (untangle findings/observables `recon_refs`) are stale when any cited id is stale in the newest snapshot.
decisions.rationale: Uses recorded evidence dependencies first and snapshot-level invalidation only where dependencies are missing, exactly as the spec requires.

decisions.question: Who owns recon query semantics, and what does remember project?
decisions.answer: recon/query.py owns query semantics as pure functions over reduced state: summary, consumers(contract), neighbors(entity, direction, depth<=max), evidence(entity), gaps(open), stale. The CLI `query` and remember both call recon code; remember never reinterprets records. remember's load_workflow passes recon reducers when replaying the recon journal and flattens the reduced state into new catalog tables recon_snapshots, recon_components, recon_contracts, recon_relationships, recon_observations, recon_gaps, each row carrying snapshot run, record revision, source revision and status. Adopted decisions stay in workflow_decisions from decisions.json; recon `decision:` refs only link.
decisions.rationale: One owner for semantics; projections are rebuildable flattenings, so rebuild-equals-replay is testable.

decisions.question: How does foundation consume recon while staying stateless?
decisions.answer: Foundation keeps no state. discover prompt (via recon.prompt) runs `orient`, then with user agreement `start`/`record`/`close` a snapshot at map depth for external contracts; the discover payload carries optional `recon_snapshot` and check_discover verifies it exists and is closed. interview prompt lists the snapshot's open gaps and asks only consequential ones. A new capability `external-contracts` (owners, schemas, compatibility/versioning, migration/deprecation documented) is assessed from the snapshot; check_assess requires every contract with unknown owner or compatibility to appear as a finding. Apply/validate are unchanged and never write recon.
decisions.rationale: Fits foundation's existing capability-based assess and stateless check functions; recon state lives in the recon journal, not in foundation.

decisions.question: How does untangle pin and use a recon snapshot, and how do its prompts stop relying on current.md/audit.json?
decisions.answer: Untangle prompts become functions of state: flow.show renders the relevant part of render_current from the journal into the printed step, so prompts stop telling agents to read current.md/audit.json (exports are still written unchanged for compatibility). Map payload requires `recon_snapshot: {"run": "snap-N"}` (closed snapshot, pinned with its revision) or `{"recon": "none", "reason": "..."}`; the ledger stores the pin. Entry points and observables may cite `recon_refs`; an observable tied to a downstream consumer's requirement is recorded as contractual (the downstream behavior constraint). Scope shows contracts and open gaps for approval; dissect findings may carry `recon_refs` and trace external effects to contract ids. On status/resume, findings and units citing stale recon ids are re-queued through the existing drift reopen path. `start --continue <audit-id>` after a published audit creates a successor run with `predecessor`, importing findings whose unit fingerprints and recon refs are unchanged. Path ledger and A/B/gap tracks are untouched.
decisions.rationale: Keeps untangle's stage graph; validated state, not exports, becomes what agents read.

decisions.question: What form does the M1 generator manifest (workflow contract draft) take?
decisions.answer: A draft at skills/_engine/policy/workflow-contract.md plus workflow-contract.schema.json describing: recon policy (none+reason|orient|map|deepen, required record types, permitted external scope, freshness), check packs (placeholder list), stages (inputs, typed outputs, evidence requirements, exit checks, transitions), budgets/checkpoints, outcomes complete|incomplete|cancelled, invocation (explicit for workflows; shared modules none). M1 writes foundation and untangle instances as test fixtures and a test that checks required keys; no runtime enforcement or generator changes until M4.
decisions.rationale: The spec asks M1 to define, not implement, the manifest; fixtures prove the existing workflows are expressible.

decisions.question: How is M1 acceptance demonstrated (fixtures, automated vs agent-driven parts, comparison report)?
decisions.answer: tests/fixtures/recon/orders (Flask-style POST /orders API, a cron ingestion job pulling an upstream vendor feed, a publisher to orders.created, shared schema schemas/order_created.v1.json, no subscriber) and tests/fixtures/recon/billing (separately supplied consumer that subscribes to orders.created and requires total_cents), plus expected-map.json. Automated (unittest): collector candidates vs expected map; scripted record sequences for repo-only (consumer unresolved + gap) and with --related billing (resolved); schema edit -> exact stale set, rest reused; decision-ref rejection for inferred patterns; remember projection rebuild equals reduced state; duplicate receipt adds nothing; chain gap/fork raise; golden version-1 journal replays identically; foundation check_discover/check_assess and untangle map/dissect checks with scripted payloads. Agent-driven: run foundation and untangle on the fixture before any change (baseline) and after, and write .agents/artifacts/v011-m1-report.md comparing both to expected-map.json with recorded cost and wall time.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic parts are tested mechanically; workflow quality is agent-driven, so it is evaluated against an explicit expected map with a baseline captured first.

decisions.question: How is the work sliced and sequenced, and which slices go through build-skills?
decisions.answer: S0 fixtures, expected map, version-1 golden journal, baseline foundation/untangle runs (direct). S1 events.replay reducers + record.accepted; recon records/validators/reducer (direct). S2 recon CLI, queries, refresh/invalidation, receipt recognition in recordings.py (direct). S3 collectors with budgets (direct). S4 workflow-contract draft + instances (direct). S5 remember projections (direct edit + tests, per D17). S6 foundation integration (build-skills revise foundation). S7 untangle integration (build-skills revise untangle). S8 install_engine copies distribution.json with `recon: 1` instead of a hardcoded dict (direct edit + test, per D17); acceptance runs, comparison report, CHANGELOG. Each slice lands with its tests; all README test commands pass after every slice.
decisions.rationale: Library first, consumers after, matching the spec's 'no engine-wide rewrite before a working consumer'; skill changes go through build-skills as the user asked.

decisions.question: What does each record type require versus leave unknown, and what are the size bounds?
decisions.answer: Every record needs id, type and classification; component, contract, relationship and observation need >=1 evidence ref unless classification=unknown. Contract requires kind, channel and direction (inbound|outbound|both); producer/consumer may be `unresolved`; owner, schema/version, compatibility, ordering, retries, idempotency, failure recovery, migration/deprecation, retention/deletion and authority boundary are optional and absent means unknown (queries print `unknown`; validators never require them). Gap requires question, searched scope, missing source/access, affected ids, consequence and next lookup. Validators cap a batch at 200 records and a statement at 500 characters; payloads must be JSON objects.
decisions.rationale: Spec: unknown fields stay unknown; bounded inputs at the trust boundary.

decisions.question: How are snapshot ids allocated and when is an existing snapshot reused instead of refreshed?
decisions.answer: `start` allocates the next `snap-N` under storage.lock on the recon state dir; the request id makes a retried start return the same run. `status` reports the newest snapshot (by predecessor chain, then N) and whether it is fresh (scope fingerprint of the primary and every related root equals the recorded one). Foundation and untangle prompts reuse a fresh closed snapshot whose depth and scope cover their need, otherwise run `refresh` (or `start` when none exists). Related roots are pinned in the snapshot with their own git HEAD/dirty fingerprint.
decisions.rationale: One rule for both consumers prevents one workflow silently re-discovering while the other reuses.

decisions.question: Do transcript receipts for recon become authoritative in M1?
decisions.answer: No. M1 makes recon receipts recognizable and replayable (replay with recon reducers, which already dedupes identical events and rejects gaps/forks), but remember projects recon only from the journal. Receipt import is exposed as non-authoritative evidence; authoritative transcript import stays the separate future migration named in the spec.
decisions.rationale: Spec allows receipts for discoverability but forbids them becoming accepted state without chain validation; deferring keeps M1 small.

decisions.question: How do untangle's audit exclusions interact with the recon snapshot scope?
decisions.answer: They stay independent. Scope shows contracts and gaps whose evidence lies inside untangle's in-scope paths, and lists the rest as outside the audit boundary; untangle never edits recon scope, and recon never adds paths to the untangle ledger.
decisions.rationale: Recon completeness never implies review coverage, and vice versa.

decisions.question: What if build-skills cannot express a revise of remember (helper-driven, not a staged workflow) or of _engine-adjacent build-skills code?
decisions.answer: Use build-skills revise sessions for foundation (S6) and untangle (S7). Edit remember's provider/catalog (S5) and build-skills' install_engine (S8) directly, with unit tests, and note the exception in the plan and CHANGELOG.
decisions.rationale: User decision 2026-11-09: build-skills only models staged and prompt skills. A prompt revise would reduce remember to SKILL.md, and extending build-skills now would pull M4 work into M1.

decisions.question: How are foundation (S6) and untangle (S7) changed, given build-skills only generates standalone skills (vendored _engine, template launcher, scripts/steps.py with PLANNING = True)?
decisions.answer: Direct edits with tests, extending D17. A build-skills revise of a bundle skill would vendor the engine (bundle guards forbid it) and force PLANNING = True on foundation's discover step, an unapproved behavior change. Teaching build-skills a bundle mode is M4 work.
decisions.rationale: User decision 2026-11-09 after a build-skills draft of foundation showed the layout conflict.

goals.goal: v0.1.1 M2 (.agents/artifacts/v011.md): add an explicitly invoked skills/review/ workflow (diff review, subsystem review, reported-bug investigation as modes of one workflow; stages frame -> recon -> obligations -> hunt -> validate -> challenge -> report, with bounded hunt/validate loops and checkpoints), reusable audit bookkeeping in skills/_engine/audit (obligation queue, evidence refs, validation attempts, dedup links, bounded transitions) with review-owned verdict rules, and targeted test analysis as checks within review, so candidates are confirmed only with a repeatable counterexample or complete source argument, test gaps stay separate from bugs, and incomplete coverage is reported honestly.
constraints: Python 3.9+, standard library only; no network; no graph DB; the script never runs project code itself; the agent runs only user-approved commands and records them.

Builds on M1 (G5 D1-D18) unchanged in contract: SQLite journal is the only authority; recon snapshots are pinned, never edited by review; recon completeness never implies review coverage; reports and exports are rebuildable views.
review is user-invoked only (disable-model-invocation, allow_implicit_invocation false); _engine/audit has no SKILL.md or trigger and never invokes a skill; review never invokes sibling skills.

Share only mechanics demonstrated by a consumer: _engine/audit is generic bookkeeping; verdict requirements live in review's domain adapter so M3 security can reuse bookkeeping without bug verdict rules. No upfront extraction of untangle logic.
Report-only: review never edits the target project; commands that may write run in an isolated worktree/temp dir; source drift of the target during a run blocks a complete report.

Coverage obligation statuses: planned, investigating, examined, blocked, deferred, not-applicable; 'examined' requires a recorded check and outcome and never means proven safe. Candidate states: proposed -> validating -> confirmed|rejected|unresolved|duplicate.

Missing tests are test gaps, not bug findings; coverage percentages are supporting evidence only; no blanket exclusion of migrations, startup, IPC or infrastructure; mutation testing only for a named uncertainty within budget.
Existing workflows (foundation, untangle, simple-by-design, build-skills, remember) keep behavior; untangle may switch to a shared recon-pin helper only if its tests and exports are unchanged.
No security workflow (M3) and no build-skills generation changes (M4); M2 may only extend the draft workflow contract (check_packs) and add a review manifest fixture.
Bundle skills are authored by direct edits with tests (precedent G5 D17/D18: build-skills cannot yet author bundle skills without vendoring _engine).
criteria: Fixture project with seeded: cross-module regression introduced by a diff, a pre-existing bug, an apparent bug neutralized by its callers, a missing test without a defect, and a test that executes code but asserts the wrong behavior, plus expected-classification.json.

Scripted runs classify each seed correctly: regression confirmed+introduced, pre-existing confirmed+pre-existing, neutralized candidate rejected with counterevidence, missing test recorded as a test gap (no finding), wrong-assertion test recorded as a test gap with evidence.

Gates refuse: confirmation without counterexample or complete source argument; 'examined' without check and outcome; rejection without counterevidence; duplicate without a target; commands not approved at frame; failed tooling counted as evidence against a claim.

Every run terminates within its budgets (hunt/validate loops, challenge rounds) via report or checkpoint; incomplete reports list blocked/deferred/excluded counts and reasons separately and are never labeled complete.
Resume after source drift reopens exactly the obligations/candidates whose cited evidence changed; stale recon citations block a complete report as in untangle.
Report regeneration from the journal is deterministic (same bytes on re-render and after replay).
All existing tests pass; review has its own unittest suite; bundle guards cover review (no vendored engine, no implicit invocation); review manifest validates against workflow-contract.schema.json.
Agent-driven evaluation on the fixture written to .agents/artifacts/v011-m2-report.md: classification vs expected, false positives, honest-uncertainty cases, and cost.

decisions.question: How is skills/review/ laid out and run (engine mode, state area, run multiplicity)?
decisions.answer: Mirror untangle: skills/review/SKILL.md (disable-model-invocation: true), agents/openai.yaml (allow_implicit_invocation: false), scripts/workflow.py launcher that finds _engine by walking up, scripts/reviewlib/{steps,checks,transitions,verdicts,report}.py, tests/. steps.MODE='stateful', AREA='review', PLANNING=True on FRAME (shared planning gates readiness, as the spec's frame exit requires a ready plan). ORDER = frame, recon, obligations, hunt, validate, challenge, report, checkpoint. One unfinished run per project (flow.start already refuses a second); commands start/status/show/abandon/done like untangle.
decisions.rationale: Existing convention for a stateful bundle skill; flow.py already gives journal-backed single-run semantics and planning gates.

decisions.question: What goes into _engine/audit versus review's domain adapter, and does untangle migrate onto it in M2?
decisions.answer: _engine/audit/ holds pure functions over plain dicts in run state: obligations.py (statuses, allowed transitions, finite queue, applicability filter over a check catalog), candidates.py (state machine proposed->validating->terminal, validation attempts list, duplicate links, reopen), evidence.py (evidence refs in recon's shape {source, path, sha256, lines, statement}, hashed by the recorder via recon.sources.file_hash; changed-ref detection), budgets.py (named counters, spend, checkpoint_to). Each terminal transition calls a domain `verdict(candidate, state)` callable passed in by the workflow; audit itself has no bug rules. review's reviewlib/verdicts.py owns bug confirmation/rejection rules. Untangle is not migrated in M2 (its work.py stays); M3 security is the second consumer that justifies any further extraction.
decisions.rationale: Spec: share only mechanics a consumer demonstrates; explicit callable keeps audit domain-free and locally readable (no registry).

decisions.question: How do the three modes (diff, subsystem, bug) frame scope, baseline and expected behavior?
decisions.answer: FRAME payload: mode diff|subsystem|bug plus a ready plan, expected behavior, scope, budgets, allowed_commands, approved_by_user. diff: {base, head} where head is a git ref or 'worktree' (uncommitted tree); script resolves refs to SHAs (git rev-parse, read-only), computes merge-base, records changed paths (git diff --name-only), and scope = changed paths plus agent-named affected callers/consumers. subsystem: path specs (file, dir, file:start-end) parsed by _engine/audit/evidence.py (untangle keeps its own ledger.parse_spec; no extraction). bug: {symptom, expected, reproduction steps or 'none', reported version/ref}; scope = suspected paths, extendable at checkpoint. All modes fingerprint in-scope files at FRAME (recon.sources.file_hash). Non-git roots allow subsystem and bug only.
decisions.rationale: One workflow, mode-specific scope preparation (spec); git reads only, never checkout in the target.

decisions.question: How does the RECON stage pin a snapshot, and is untangle's reconview pin logic shared?
decisions.answer: Move untangle's mode-neutral recon helpers (pin, snapshot, fresh_refs, stale) into _engine/recon/pin.py taking a `need` error callable and a root; untangle/workflowlib/reconview.py keeps its scope-specific views (contracts inside/outside audit boundary) and calls pin.py. Review's RECON stage payload: recon_snapshot 'snap-N' (closed) or recon_none reason, identical to untangle MAP. Prompt includes recon guide.prompt and suggests map depth around the scope; deepen only for gaps an obligation needs. Untangle tests and exports must stay byte-identical.
decisions.rationale: Pin logic now has two consumers; one owner prevents drift. Allowed by constraint when untangle stays unchanged.

decisions.question: How are obligations shaped, kept finite, and selected without a file-by-check Cartesian product (check catalog and applicability)?
decisions.answer: Obligation = {id, target (path spec, flow, or recon id), risk, check (catalog id), rationale, status, outcome?, evidence[]}. Check catalog = JSON packs in _engine/audit/checks/: general.json (compatibility, lifecycle/cleanup, concurrency, error propagation, resource bounds, input validation at boundary), tests.json (D9), python.json (async cancellation, subprocess, exception swallowing, mutable defaults, ORM transaction scope). Each check: id, pack, version, applies {languages[], boundaries[], modes[]}, evidence_required, falsifiers, validation_methods, limits. OBLIGATIONS gate: every obligation names a catalog check whose `applies` matches the target's language/boundary; total <= budget max_obligations (suggest 2x scope units, hard cap 200); each has rationale; script rejects duplicates (same target+check). Languages in scope without a pack become a recorded coverage gap (unsupported scope), never silently skipped. not-applicable requires reason.
decisions.rationale: Agent selects relevant pairs with rationale under a hard cap, so no Cartesian product; catalog as data is shared with M3 and fits workflow-contract check_packs.

decisions.question: How does HUNT advance through obligations, and how are hunt/validate loops bounded?
decisions.answer: HUNT `done` reports on one or more obligations from the queue head (max hunt_batch, default 5): each moves to examined (check performed + outcome + evidence), blocked (reason), deferred (reason) or not-applicable (reason), and may propose candidates linked to it. Candidates go to the VALIDATE queue; after the obligation queue empties or a batch ends with proposed candidates, next stage is VALIDATE; VALIDATE may spawn variant obligations (budget variant_obligations) which return to HUNT. Budgets (all finite, approved at FRAME): hunt_transitions, validate_transitions, attempts_per_candidate, variant_obligations, challenge_rounds, max_obligations. Spending any one routes to CHECKPOINT (extend with user approval, publish_incomplete, or reframe), like untangle.
decisions.rationale: Batching keeps turns proportional; explicit counters guarantee termination.

decisions.question: What is a candidate, and what evidence gates each terminal state (confirmed, rejected, unresolved, duplicate), including diff-mode origin?
decisions.answer: Candidate = {id, obligation, expected (contract/invariant text + recon id or evidence), actual, trigger, affected sources (evidence), counterevidence[], state, attempts[], verdict}. Terminal gates in reviewlib/verdicts.py: confirmed needs proof.kind = counterexample {command (approved), revision, exit, observed output digest+excerpt, repeatable: true} or source_argument {steps: ordered claims each with evidence, covering trigger -> fault -> observable effect; mitigations_checked: callers/guards examined with evidence}; rejected needs >=1 counterevidence ref (e.g. caller guard) with statement; duplicate needs duplicate_of an existing non-duplicate candidate; unresolved needs reason and attempts listing what was tried (tool failure lands here, never in counterevidence). Diff mode: confirmed also needs origin introduced|pre-existing|unknown; introduced/pre-existing require baseline evidence (file content at merge-base read via `git show <sha>:path`, hashed by the script, or a counterexample run at baseline in an isolated worktree); unknown requires reason. Severity (high|medium|low) and confidence are separate fields.
decisions.rationale: Spec's confirmation rule made mechanical: script checks structure and hashes, agent supplies reasoning.

decisions.question: How are commands approved, recorded and isolated so the target is never edited and failed tooling is not counter-evidence?
decisions.answer: allowed_commands approved at FRAME (default none = static analysis), each with exact argv string, purpose and declared side effects, extendable only at CHECKPOINT with approved_by_user. Every recorded run: {command, cwd kind: worktree|tempdir, base revision, env notes, exit, output sha256 + <=2000-char excerpt}; the gate rejects commands not in the list and cwd = target root. Prompt instructs `git worktree add <scratch> <sha>` (or copy to temp dir for non-git) and removal afterwards; the script never runs them. Drift guard: before VALIDATE->CHALLENGE and at REPORT the script re-fingerprints in-scope files; any change blocks a complete report (checkpoint 'drift'). Exit !=0 because of tooling (missing dep, timeout) is recorded as attempt outcome tool-failed -> candidate stays validating/unresolved.
decisions.rationale: Same permission model as untangle; isolation enforced by recording + fingerprint check since the script cannot sandbox the agent.

decisions.question: How is targeted test analysis represented (test gaps vs candidates) and which test checks ship?
decisions.answer: Test analysis is checks in tests.json applied as obligations: contract->test exists, assertion meaningful (asserts the contract, not incidental output), setup fidelity (mocks match real boundary), CI execution (test is collected and run by CI config, not skipped/xfail), negative/failure path, lifecycle/recovery, flaky markers. Outcomes are TestGap records {id, contract, chain_break: no-test|no-assertion|wrong-assertion|unrealistic-setup|not-in-ci|skipped|flaky, evidence, consequence}, stored separately from candidates and never counted as findings. A wrong-assertion test that also hides a real defect yields both a test gap and a separate candidate. Mutation testing allowed only as a validation attempt with `uncertainty` named, an approved command, and within attempts_per_candidate. Coverage numbers may be attached as evidence only.
decisions.rationale: Spec: missing tests are gaps, not bugs; keeps one obligation mechanism.

decisions.question: How are source drift and resume handled (pinned fingerprints, reopening exactly affected items)?
decisions.answer: status/resume and the CHALLENGE/REPORT gates compare current hashes of every evidence path cited by obligations, candidates and test gaps (plus FRAME fingerprints). Items citing a changed/vanished file are reopened (obligation -> planned, candidate -> proposed with attempts kept, confirmed verdict cleared) and requeued; items without changed citations keep state. Stale recon citations (via _engine/recon/pin.stale) block a complete report and route to checkpoint 'recon stale'. In diff mode a moved head ref is drift: checkpoint offers reframe.
decisions.rationale: Reopen exactly what cited changed evidence; same conservative rule as M1 D6.
